Both backends are measured because both ship, and M4.1 measured them identical
to three decimal places on every metric — that equality is the parity contract,
not a coincidence. `leaks` is a hard zero, not a target: a superseded or
cross-scope object surfacing at all is a correctness failure, and hit rate
bought by also returning the stale answer is not a win.
M4.1 moved these by fixing candidate generation, not the blend — ranking_version
is still 1.0. A superseded object is now a candidate and is redirected to what
replaced it, and `restricted` objects are excluded. hit@1 and paraphrase each
cost a little: a correction inherits its ancestor's relevance to unrelated
queries. Damping that was tried across 1.0-0.75 and bought nothing on this
suite, so it was not shipped. A real embedder erases both costs (paraphrase is
100% on nomic-embed-text), which is where the residual belongs.
